rationale: The workflow runs `nuget restore` on every pull request, repeatedly fetching NuGet dependencies. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache mechanism) is supported by observational evidence reporting modest aggregate VM-time reduction from caching dependency downloads. Its preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable (nuget restore executes each run), and cache inputs can be keyed to the solution/project/package manifest files as a proxy for a lockfile plus runner environment. Adding an actions/cache step before `nuget restore` preserves all build and test coverage unchanged—no step is removed, skipped, or altered—and introduces no new network access, secrets, privileged actions, or publishing/deployment operations. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT was considered but not applied because the repository CI history shows only failed runs, so the precondition of representative successful-duration history is not met and a safe timeout cannot be derived.
